title: Fluent full technical rebrand
objective: Replace every repository-level Fluent identifier, file and directory with Fluent equivalents, migrate the exact existing local application-data directory and database name without changing their bytes, and preserve the established local-first, authentication and Cloud safety behavior.

included: Mechanical case-preserving replacements Fluent→Fluent, fluent→fluent and FLUENT→FLUENT in repository text sources, documentation, tests, project files, solution metadata, scripts and history_session.md, excluding generated and protected material

Explicit rename of the solution, 28 discovered Fluent-named files, all Fluent-named source/test/tool directories, and the two enclosing repository directories from C:/SECOND_BRAIN/PROJECTS/Fluent/Fluent to C:/SECOND_BRAIN/PROJECTS/Fluent/Fluent
Namespace, assembly, project-reference, test-name, resource and output-name migration necessary for Fluent.sln to build

Read-only exact pre/post manifest and SHA-256 baseline/final verification for C:/Users/exhorte/AppData/Local/Fluent including fluent.db and any SQLite sidecars, followed by exact same-parent Rename-Item steps to C:/Users/exhorte/AppData/Local/Fluent and fluent.db only when the destination is absent, both paths resolve to the same volume and Fluent/Fluent are not running
Evidence, architecture, privacy, state, roadmap, risk and history updates plus full restore/build/test and final Judge review
excluded: Reading, printing, modifying, committing or loading .env, .env.*, credentials, API keys, tokens, certificates, account data, secret configuration or database contents
.git metadata, Git remote configuration, git add/commit/push/pull/reset/clean/checkout/switch, GitHub, Supabase, Google, DeepSeek, browser settings, deployment, billing or live provider invocation
bin, obj, package caches, Visual Studio caches and any generated artifact; they must be recreated only by allowed build commands

Any semantic behavior, security guard, API contract, authentication flow, user data content, SQLite schema, Whisper model contents, audio, history payload or configuration value beyond renaming identifier/path labels

Overwriting a pre-existing C:/Users/exhorte/AppData/Local/Fluent directory or performing a local-data move if a source lock, live Fluent/Fluent process, same-volume precondition or hash mismatch is detected
Opening, querying, modifying, vacuuming, copying, deleting, restoring from backup or otherwise changing SQLite, model or user-data bytes

allowedCommandFamilies: powershell read-only process inspection, manifest collection and volume/path checks
powershell explicit same-parent Rename-Item only after resolved path, destination, process, manifest and volume checks

No case-insensitive Fluent identifier remains in repository text/source files after excluding .git, bin and obj; no Fluent-named file or directory remains inside the renamed repository.

The local SQLite database and every present SQLite sidecar have equal before/after SHA-256 hashes, Models remains present, the destination was absent before migration and no user data content is opened or altered.
Existing local-first, authentication, Cloud, DeepSeek-disabled-by-default-configuration, target safety and privacy controls retain their behavior after identifier migration.
history_session.md is updated to record the controlled technical migration without inventing external configuration or test evidence.
Restore, Release build, complete test suite, rename scans, diff check, reviews and final Judge evidence pass; status remains IMPLEMENTED_AWAITING_USER_REVIEW.
No secret access, external account mutation, provider call, deployment or Git mutation occurs.
requiredTests: Pre/post full-repository case-insensitive identifier and filename/directory scans excluding .git, bin and obj

Local-data source/destination and same-volume preflight; Fluent/Fluent process and lock check; exact pre/post directory manifests; SHA-256 equality for database/sidecars; Models presence; source-path disappearance after exact rename
git diff --check and full test regression
risks: A partial rename can break solution references, namespaces, WPF XAML type names, test discovery or build output.
A broad text replacement can alter protected/configuration/generated material or historical evidence incorrectly.
A local application-data move can lose user dictionary access, overwrite data, fail under a lock or alter database bytes.
An interruption after the directory rename but before every database filename rename can leave a mixed path state unless the recorded state machine is followed.
An external service or Git reference can be changed unintentionally while trying to complete a repository rebrand.

The source project/test/tool directories carry the NTFS ReadOnly attribute and currently block Rename-Item; any attribute adjustment must be captured, exact-path-only, reversible and followed by the same target attribute after a successful rename.
rollbackPlan: Use the recorded explicit reverse rename mapping before any Git mutation.
State S0 (no mutation): source stays C:/Users/exhorte/AppData/Local/Fluent if any preflight condition fails.

State S1 (directory renamed): if a database/sidecar rename fails, reverse only completed file renames then Rename-Item C:/Users/exhorte/AppData/Local/Fluent back to C:/Users/exhorte/AppData/Local/Fluent, but only if each reverse destination is absent.

State S2 (all names renamed): if post-migration manifest or hash verification fails, reverse exact database/sidecar filenames then the directory name, subject to absent reverse destinations; otherwise stop without overwrite and report the exact unresolved state.
Restore no content from backups because this task never rewrites database or model bytes.

openFindings: A detected running Fluent/Fluent process, source lock, destination conflict, different-volume condition, missing source, manifest/hash mismatch or failed rollback precondition blocks the local-data move rather than overwrite or retry destructively.

executionAmendments.reason: All 18 static source project/test/tool directories were observed with the NTFS ReadOnly attribute, and Rename-Item is denied before any directory move.
scope: A0: before every mapping, verify the exact static source/target pair, source-directory presence, target absence, no unresolved parent/child ordering conflict, and capture the complete source Attributes value.
A1: remove only the ReadOnly bit from that one source directory without recursion, then reread the source Attributes value to verify that all remaining bits are unchanged.
A2: perform the exact Rename-Item only after A0/A1 verification succeeds.
A3: verify source absent and target present, apply the complete captured Attributes value to the target directory, then reread it to prove equality.
If a failure occurs before A2, restore and verify the complete captured Attributes value on the unchanged source, then stop.
If a failure occurs after A2, do not attempt to recreate or overwrite the absent source. Stop in the recorded target-path state, preserve evidence and require a new decision for recovery.
Do not alter ACLs, ownership, inherited permissions, files, data, Git, secrets or generated contents.
executionAmendments.rollback: Before A2 only, restore the captured attribute to the unchanged source and verify equality. After A2, no automatic reverse rename occurs; the target-path state is preserved without overwrite and requires a new reviewed recovery decision.
